documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up note (copy to PCP)

Six-month follow-up for prolactinoma on cabergoline. Over the last three months she has lost weight without trying and has been hot when others are not, with frequent pounding heartbeats. Cycles remain irregular, as they have been for about six months.

HR 108.
Thyroid diffusely enlarged and non-tender. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands at rest. Mild lid lag on both sides with some swelling around the eyes.

TSH low.

Assessment: Graves disease.
Plan: methimazole 10 mg daily started. Labs in 4-6 weeks. Continue cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly. Return in 6 months, sooner if symptoms worsen.

documents.title: New thyroid medicine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, endo started me on methimazole for Graves. They said I need bloodwork in about a month to check my blood counts and liver and that you could draw it here since it's closer to school. Is that ok? Also the heart pounding is a little better already.

documents.title: RE: New thyroid medicine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, of course. I put in a CBC and liver panel - come any morning the week of Feb 22. With methimazole, if you get a fever or a sore throat, stop it and call us the same day so we can check your white count. Glad the palpitations are easing.

documents.title: Methimazole monitoring labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC with diff and LFTs normal, neutrophils fine. Copy faxed to endocrinology. Pt notified via portal.

documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got both Pfizer doses through the educator clinic, 2/27 and 3/20. Photo of my card attached. Just a sore arm and a tired day after the second.

documents.title: RE: COVID vaccine card
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Morgan, both doses are entered in your record.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in after school. Pollen season, using albuterol a few times a week the last 3 weeks, mostly after recess duty outside. Sleeping through the night, no night cough. Never needed urgent care.

Thyroid: on methimazole since January per endo, weight coming back up, palpitations gone. Cabergoline continues. No seizures.

Vitals as charted. Lungs clear, no wheeze today, normal effort. Heart regular, not fast. No tremor.

A/P
Asthma - seasonal, intermittent. New albuterol script (old one from prior office). Rinse/shower after yard duty helps some people. Return if needing it daily.
Epilepsy - phenytoin level today.
Graves/prolactinoma - per endo.

documents.title: Phenytoin level
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Level 15.6, right where we want it. No change.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No-show for 7:40 physical. Called, left voicemail. Pt texted back - parent-teacher conferences were moved to this morning, forgot to cancel. Rebooked 10/19.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical (rebooked from 10/5).

Doing well. Graves treated since Jan, endo saw her this summer - stable, staying on methimazole 10. Cabergoline twice weekly. Periods still not like clockwork. Asthma fine after June, rescue inhaler rarely. No seizures.

Meds: phenytoin 300 daily, methimazole 10 daily, cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly, albuterol prn.
Allergies: pollen.

Exam: vitals reviewed, weight up a bit. Eyes look comfortable, no stare. Thyroid smooth, maybe slightly full. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No tremor. Skin normal.
PHQ-2: 1.

Plan: flu today. Pap is due - she'd rather do it on a separate day; will plan at next physical (she knows it's overdue by a year). Booster when eligible. Labs and phenytoin level.

documents.title: Booster
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got my booster Saturday at the pharmacy (Pfizer). Labs from the physical came through on the app, all looked normal to me?

documents.title: RE: Booster
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Booster recorded. Yes, all normal, phenytoin 13.1.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology - follow-up visit note

Prolactinoma and Graves disease, on cabergoline and methimazole.

For several months she has felt restless and irritable and sleeps poorly. She has lost 10 lb over the past 3 months although she is eating well. Her sister came with her today and told us privately that Morgan has become very focused on her appearance and has been taking triiodothyronine tablets ordered online. Morgan denies chest pain, tremor and any recent illness.

HR 106, BP 132/76.
Anxious-appearing, alert and cooperative. Thyroid not palpable, no tenderness or enlargement. No lid lag, no proptosis, no pretibial edema.

Assessment: thyrotoxic symptoms; exogenous T3 vs. endogenous source.
Plan: thyroid function panel and pituitary hormone labs, radioactive iodine uptake scan, and repeat pituitary MRI. Results letter to follow.

conditions.label: Secondary hyperthyroidism due to TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma

documents.title: Endocrinology results letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Workup for Ms. Sheehan's thyrotoxic symptoms is back:
- Free T4 2.4 ng/dL (high) with TSH 3.6 mIU/L, i.e. TSH not suppressed.
- Radioactive iodine uptake 52% at 24 hours, diffuse.
- Pituitary MRI: the adenoma now measures 11 mm. It does not reach the optic chiasm.

A normal-range TSH alongside a high free T4 and high diffuse uptake is not what exogenous T3 would produce. We now consider this a plurihormonal pituitary macroadenoma secreting prolactin and TSH, with secondary hyperthyroidism.

I discussed the online T3 with her and she has agreed to stop it. She is to continue cabergoline 0.5 mg twice weekly and methimazole 10 mg daily. We will see her in 6 months with labs.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Endo letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I saw the endo letter got sent to you. I want you to know I threw the pills out. I'm a little embarrassed about it. Do I need to do anything different with you?

documents.title: RE: Endo letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and no need to be embarrassed - I'm glad it's out of the house. Nothing different on our end; keep going with endo's plan and your usual meds. If you're ever feeling pressure about weight or how you look, I'm happy to talk about that any time.

documents.body: Refill request albuterol HFA. Last fill Nov. Pollen season, pt says using a few times a week, no nighttime symptoms. Sent 1 inhaler + 1 refill.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical + Pap.

Feels much better than last winter. Off the online T3 since February. Endo now calls the pituitary tumor a macroadenoma that makes both prolactin and TSH; plan from them is to stay on cabergoline and methimazole. She saw them in August, says labs were good. Periods regular every 28-30 days since spring. Weight up from the winter. Sleeping. Asthma quiet. No seizures.

She and her husband are thinking about trying for a pregnancy in the next year - she'll ask endo about the cabergoline and methimazole timing. I mentioned we'd want her on a prenatal vitamin once they start trying.

Meds: phenytoin 300 daily, methimazole 10 daily, cabergoline 0.5 twice weekly, albuterol prn.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Thyroid normal size, no nodules. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV collected. Skin fine.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Oligomenorrhea resolved; cycles regular.
- Pituitary macroadenoma / TSH-driven hyperthyroidism / Graves: endo.
- Epilepsy: level today.
- HM: Pap/HPV today, flu today, bivalent COVID at pharmacy.
- Preconception: talk with endo, and with us when ready.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pap normal and HPV negative - next one in 5 years. Labs normal, phenytoin 14.9.
